subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory preserve OpenClaw's documented OGG/Opus support by transcoding to MP3/WAV, or should OpenClaw narrow Gemini audio support to raw MP3/WAV with skip diagnostics and docs?
rationale: Both outcomes fix the 400 error, but they set different user-facing contracts and operator dependencies for memory indexing.

options.title: Preserve support with transcode
options.body: Keep OGG/Opus in the supported memory-audio contract, reuse the existing media-runtime/ffmpeg path to normalize unsupported Gemini audio to MP3 or WAV, and emit a clear skip diagnostic if transcoding is unavailable.

options.title: Narrow Gemini audio formats
options.body: Remove or provider-filter unsupported Gemini audio formats so OGG/Opus are skipped before API calls, then update docs to say Gemini memory audio accepts only MP3/WAV raw inputs.

options.title: Design provider format metadata first
options.body: Pause the fix until memory embedding providers expose per-modality supported formats, then make scanning/filtering/transcoding data-driven across providers.

recommendation.title: Preserve support with transcode
recommendation.body: Keep OGG/Opus in the supported memory-audio contract, reuse the existing media-runtime/ffmpeg path to normalize unsupported Gemini audio to MP3 or WAV, and emit a clear skip diagnostic if transcoding is unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: The original multimodal memory indexing author is the strongest history signal for the intended user-facing format contract.
